basics.name: Laser-cutting joint guides and generators: MakerCase (web box generator), kerf-bending living hinge patterns (Obrary swatches, Deferred Procrastination lattice-hinge maths, buxtronix Inkscape extension) and Ponoko's laser-cut joint guides
basics.url: https://www.makercase.com/ (generator; help articles served at https://www.makercase.com/markdown/kerf-calibrate.md, /markdown/kerf-bent.md, /markdown/download.md, /markdown/polygon.md). Hinge patterns: https://obrary.com/products/living-hinge-patterns and https://obrary.com/products/living-hinge-pattern-fabric (files at https://github.com/Obrary/Living-Hinge-Swatches, README read via raw.githubusercontent.com); http://marksabino.com/defproc/blog/2011/laser-cut-lattice-living-hinges/ and http://marksabino.com/defproc/blog/2012/minimum-bend-radius/ (Patrick Fenner's lattice hinge maths); https://github.com/buxtronix/living-hinge (Inkscape extension, read via raw.githubusercontent.com). Ponoko: https://www.ponoko.com/blog/how-to-make/how-to-design-a-living-hinge/, https://www.ponoko.com/blog/how-to-make/how-much-material-does-the-laser-burn-away/, https://www.ponoko.com/blog/how-to-make/how-to-make-glue-less-interlocking-parts/, https://help.ponoko.com/en/articles/4527166-interlocking-3d-laser-cut-designs
basics.resource_type: Mixed: interactive tool (MakerCase web generator; buxtronix Inkscape extension), PDF/CAD pattern library (Obrary living hinge swatches as DXF/PDF/SketchUp) and maker design guides (Ponoko blog and help centre, Deferred Procrastination blog)
basics.cost: MakerCase: free for its 'classic' generators with no sign-up (non-commercial use only); a free account gives 3 downloads a month from its 'pro' generators; Pro is $10/year (unlimited downloads, no ads, offline access, commercial licence); a Site Licence for schools and makerspaces is $99/year. Obrary swatches, Deferred Procrastination posts, the Inkscape extension and Ponoko guides are free
basics.license: Mixed. MakerCase: proprietary web app; its plan table says free tiers are for non-commercial use only and Pro adds a 'commercial license' for what you make (no open licence for the site or its help images). Obrary Living Hinge Swatches and koFAKTORlab 'Living Hinge Pattern - Fabric': Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 (CC BY-SA 4.0), so the DXF patterns and images can be reused with credit and share-alike. buxtronix living-hinge Inkscape extension: GPL v3. Ponoko pages: '(c)2022 Ponoko Limited. All rights reserved', so link only. Deferred Procrastination posts: no licence stated, so treat as all rights reserved and link only
basics.language: English. The MakerCase interface is also translated (the app bundle contains German, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Korean, Chinese, Persian, Hebrew and Hindi strings); its help articles are English only
basics.year: Ponoko kerf guide 11 September 2008 (figures flagged by the author as out of date); Deferred Procrastination lattice hinge posts 16 December 2011 and 9 November 2012; MakerCase copyright '(c)2012-2026', about page 'Updated September 21, 2026'; Obrary Living Hinge Patterns v1.0 September 2014; Ponoko glue-less interlocking parts 27 February 2015 and living hinge guide 6 July 2015; Ponoko help-centre interlocking designs article 5 November 2020
basics.access_barrier: none for reading the guides, downloading Obrary files or using MakerCase classic generators; free login (and then a download cap) for MakerCase 'pro' generators; desktop install of Inkscape for the living-hinge extension; SketchUp for the Obrary .skp model (DXF/PDF need no special software)
basics.image_license: Obrary swatch photos and files: CC BY-SA 4.0 (stated on the product pages). buxtronix README sample swatch images sit in a GPL v3 repo. MakerCase tutorial photos and Ponoko images: all rights reserved (no licence shown), link only. Deferred Procrastination diagrams: no licence stated [uncertain]
basics.authority_level: community or unvetted, plus manufacturer: Ponoko is a commercial laser-cutting service writing from production experience; MakerCase is a long-running maker tool by one developer (Jon Hollander); Obrary was a community open-design marketplace; Deferred Procrastination is an engineer's blog with worked equations. None is peer-reviewed

coverage.covers: Flat-pack joints for laser-cut sheet parts and the kerf (the width the laser burns away) that makes them fit. MakerCase generates whole boxes in 9 generators (Basic Box, Curved/kerf-bent Box, Custom Divider Box, Divider Box, Laser Hinge Box, Polygon Box, Sliding Lid Box, Stackable Parts Bin, Basic 3D Printed Box) with three edge-joint choices: flat edges, finger joints (box joints) and T-slot joints (bolt-and-captive-nut slots with bolt size, length and count settings); plus kerf compensation for lasers and dogbone corner fillets for CNC routers. Living hinges (kerf bending / lattice hinges): Obrary gives two swatch sets, one comparing several hinge patterns and one showing the straight pattern at different spacings, plus a double-curvature 'fabric' pattern; Deferred Procrastination explains why lattice hinges work (thin links twisting in torsion) and gives formulas for link count and bend radius; the buxtronix extension draws straight, diamond and cross lattice patterns. Ponoko covers kerf and press fits (sizing a square and its hole so they 'click' together), glue-less interlocking slot parts with 'nodes' (crush bumps), corner radii for acrylic slots, slot allowance cuts for hard plastics, bolt-and-nut T-slot fastening, clips, and living hinge design. Roughly 15-20 distinct joint and hinge types in total across the group
coverage.organisation: Scattered and tool-first. MakerCase is organised by the box you want (basic, polygon, hinge, sliding lid, curved, divider, stackable bin), with joints chosen from a drop-down; four step-by-step help articles (kerf calibration, download settings, kerf-bent boxes, polygon boxes). Obrary is a product-page catalogue of downloadable designs. Ponoko's material is a set of standalone blog posts and help-centre articles with no joint index. Deferred Procrastination is a chronological blog series (introduction, test results, torsional stress, minimum bend radius). Works for someone who already knows they want 'a box' or 'a living hinge'; there is no way to browse by joint type or by problem
coverage.scope_match: medium: squarely inside the project's laser-cut joinery family (lowest priority by making method) and includes several clever types (kerf-tolerant press fits with crush nodes, T-slot captive nut joints, lattice living hinges including double-curvature ones, sliding lids, stacking tabs). But most of it is box generation and kerf calibration rather than a catalogue of connection types, and it has nothing on the project's special behaviours beyond compliant hinges
coverage.taxonomy_used: No formal taxonomy. MakerCase: 3 edge-joint types (flat, finger, T-slot) crossed with 9 box generators. Living hinges: grouped by cut pattern (straight lattice, diamond lattice, cross lattice, fabric/spiral double-curvature) and by spacing. Ponoko: grouped by fit technique (kerf-sized press fit, nodes/crush ribs, radii, slot allowances, bolts/T-slots, clips)
coverage.example_types: finger joint (box joint); T-slot joint (captive nut and bolt slot); flat butt edge (baseline glued edge); kerf-compensated press fit (tolerance-fit square and hole); slot joint with nodes (crush-bump friction fit, kerf-tolerant); slot with corner radii (crack-resistant slot for acrylic); slot allowance cuts (flexing relief around slots in hard plastic); interlocking cross-slot (egg-crate / slice-form) joint; laser-cut clip (sheet snap tab); lattice living hinge, straight pattern (kerf-bending torsion hinge); diamond lattice hinge; cross lattice hinge; double-curvature 'fabric' living hinge (spiral slit pattern); kerf-bent rounded box corner; sliding lid in grooves; laser-cut pin hinge box (Laser Hinge Box with pivot diameter setting) [uncertain for exact hinge style]; interlocking stacking tabs (stackable bin); dogbone corner fillet (router-bit relief for square tabs)
coverage.making_methods: Laser cutting of sheet material (plywood, MDF, acrylic, Delrin, card); MakerCase also targets CNC routers (dogbone fillets) and has one 3D-printed box generator
coverage.item_count: MakerCase: 9 generators, 3 edge-joint types, 4 help articles. Obrary: 2 living hinge swatch sets plus 1 fabric pattern (Obrary's laser collection holds about 105 designs over 7 pages, most not joint-specific). Deferred Procrastination: about 4 lattice-hinge posts. buxtronix extension: 3 lattice patterns. Ponoko: about 4 relevant guides
coverage.special_behaviours_covered: Compliant: yes, living (lattice) hinges and kerf bending are the main compliant topic, with Deferred Procrastination's torsion-based design maths and Obrary's flexibility comparison swatches. Snap / self-locking: only lightly (Ponoko's nodes make parts 'snap and lock into place'; 'clips' mentioned without rules). Indexing/detent, one-way/ratchet, torque-limiting, over-centre, hand-release-only, print-in-place, gear trains, powered connectors: none. Adhesives: only in passing (MakerCase tutorials use wood glue and painter's tape to clamp; Ponoko and MakerCase pitch glue-less press fits as the alternative)
coverage.entry_structure: MakerCase: parameter form (inside/outside dimensions, material thickness, joint type, finger size, bolt size/length/count for T-slots, number of bends and bend radius for kerf-bent boxes), live rotatable 3D preview, download dialog with labels, line colours, kerf or dogbone compensation. Obrary: product page with photos, description, licence and ZIP of DXF, PDF and SketchUp files. Ponoko/Deferred Procrastination: illustrated article with photos, a few numbers or formulas, and sometimes downloadable test files
coverage.audience_level: hobbyist (makerspace laser users and people ordering from a laser-cutting service); Deferred Procrastination's maths is undergraduate engineering level

usefulness.beginner_friendliness: high for MakerCase (enter a size, pick a joint, download; its kerf calibration article walks through cutting a 1 inch test square, measuring with calipers and entering half the kerf, with 'too tight: decrease kerf, too loose: increase kerf'); medium for Ponoko (plain language but few numbers); low for Deferred Procrastination (torsion formulas)
usefulness.has_images: yes: MakerCase help articles have step photos of real boxes and screenshots; Obrary has photos of cut swatches; Ponoko has photos of hinges and a trivet made with node joints; Deferred Procrastination has diagrams of junctions and spring connections. No consistent labelled diagram set of joint types
usefulness.has_animations: MakerCase has an interactive rotatable 3D box preview; the Ponoko kerf post embeds a video of a press-fit part clicking in; buxtronix extension offers Inkscape live preview. No animations of joints in use
usefulness.gaps: No joint-type catalogue: joints are options inside box generators or topics of separate blog posts. Few numbers for snap tabs, clips or press-fit interference; strength and durability of living hinges not quantified beyond Deferred Procrastination's acrylic calculations. Ponoko's kerf tables are from 2008 and flagged as outdated. Nothing on choosing between joint types, on reversible or hand-release joints, or on the project's special behaviours. MakerCase pro generators now sit behind a download cap
usefulness.good_for_entry_links: partly. Stable per-item pages exist for Obrary designs (e.g. https://obrary.com/products/living-hinge-patterns), Ponoko posts (e.g. https://www.ponoko.com/blog/how-to-make/how-to-design-a-living-hinge/) and Deferred Procrastination posts (e.g. http://marksabino.com/defproc/blog/2012/minimum-bend-radius/). MakerCase generator pages are single-page-app routes and its help articles are best linked as raw markdown files (e.g. https://www.makercase.com/markdown/kerf-calibrate.md), which is fragile
usefulness.reusable_data: Obrary hinge swatches are reusable under CC BY-SA 4.0 (DXF/PDF/SKP in a GitHub repo); the buxtronix hinge generator is GPL v3 code. MakerCase and Ponoko are not reusable beyond linking (proprietary, all rights reserved); lists of joint names can be restated as facts
usefulness.maintained: MakerCase: actively maintained (about page updated 21 September 2026, new subscription tiers and translations). Ponoko: guides still online; help-centre article from 2020; blog posts from 2008-2015 with 2022 copyright footer. Obrary: product pages still online; hinge files date from 2014-2016. Deferred Procrastination: old blog (2011-2012) now hosted under marksabino.com/defproc; buxtronix extension still on GitHub (supports Inkscape 1.0+)
usefulness.ideas_to_borrow: (1) A 'kerf test square' calibration step linked from every sheet-joint entry, with the simple rule 'too tight: decrease kerf, too loose: increase kerf'. (2) Obrary-style swatch cards: one cut sheet showing several variants side by side so makers can feel stiffness before committing (also works for 3D-printed snap fits and flexures). (3) Deferred Procrastination's plain explanation of a lattice hinge as many small torsion springs, plus a link-count and bend-radius formula, as a model for 'why it works' boxes. (4) MakerCase's joint drop-down (flat / finger / T-slot) as a tiny decision point in the flow chart: glue only, press fit, or bolted and removable. (5) Ponoko's material-specific advice (nodes for soft wood, radii for brittle acrylic, slot allowances for hard plastic) as a 'material tweaks' field on each entry
usefulness.design_rules_given: Yes, a few. MakerCase: default kerf compensation 0.25 mm (beam diameter / 2), enter half the measured kerf; suggested minimum bend radius computed from plywood properties for kerf-bent boxes, with advice to use thinner stock or taller boxes for tighter bends; dogbone fillet sized from router bit diameter. Ponoko: kerf typically 0.08-0.15 mm (search summary, not verified on the page) [uncertain]; material thickness can vary by about 10 percent; MDF and Delrin more consistent than plywood or acrylic. Deferred Procrastination: for 3 mm acrylic bent 90 degrees, links needed fall from 22 (5 mm connection length) to 4 (30 mm length); with 0.2 mm kerf, 23 links give an inner bend radius of 44 mm and outer 47 mm; formulas n >= angle / (pi/4 - acos((kerf + t) / (2 sqrt(t^2/2)))) and r_inner = 2W/angle - t/2
usefulness.generator_or_parametric: Yes: MakerCase is a parametric web generator for boxes (and outputs kerf/dogbone-compensated files); the buxtronix Inkscape extension generates straight, diamond and cross lattice hinge patterns to fill any shape and can draw a swatch card. Obrary and Ponoko provide fixed files and guidance only
usefulness.file_formats: MakerCase: SVG and DXF (with configurable cut line colours and widths). Obrary: DXF, PDF and SketchUp (.skp) in a ZIP. buxtronix: Inkscape extension (.inx/.py) producing SVG. Ponoko/Deferred Procrastination: web articles with photos, some downloadable test files
usefulness.terminology_value: medium: good source for maker names and aliases of kerf-bending hinges ('living hinge', 'lattice hinge', 'kerf bending', 'flexure'), 'nodes' as the laser-cut name for crush ribs, 'T-slot' for captive-nut joints and 'dogbone' corner fillets. No translations or formal engineering names
usefulness.decision_support: Minimal. MakerCase's joint drop-down (flat, finger, T-slot) and its bend-radius suggestion are the only choice aids; Obrary swatches let makers compare flexibility physically; Ponoko gives material-based advice (nodes for wood, radii for acrylic). No flow chart, filters or comparison tables
usefulness.derived_from_or_overlaps: Heavy overlap with Boxes.py (already researched: finger, T-slot-like bed bolts, flex cuts, sliding lids, hinges) and with the HCI research tools SpringFit and Joinery (already researched: kerf-tolerant press fits and spring joints). The lattice hinge itself originated with Snijlab, a Dutch laser-cutting workshop (Deferred Procrastination, 2011); Ponoko's living hinge guide cites Deferred Procrastination and Martin Breuer's pattern tests. Ponoko's help article points readers to MakerCase and Thingiverse. Make: magazine's 'CNC Panel Joinery Notebook' (Sean Michael Ragan, 2012) catalogues many of the same sheet joints plus kanelba hinges and sninges
